'''Akitomi Shrine''' (あきとみじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Higashibaba, Iitomi, {{ill|Sodegaura|Q646847|qid=Q646847}}, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|Q80011|qid=Q80011}}.

===Origin===
It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} whose name already appears in the “{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Sandai Jitsuroku}}” and the “{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}},” compiled during the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, and is an ancient shrine that has existed for more than a thousand years. Its former name was Otomi Shrine, and it is the only Shikinaisha in the Kimitsu region, making it of high historical value.

According to shrine tradition, it was founded in the first year of the reign of the second emperor, {{ill|Emperor Suizei|Q313321|qid=Q313321}}, by the emperor’s elder brother {{ill|Kamuyaimimi|Q11588756|qid=Q11588756}}. The principal enshrined deity is Ukanomitama no Mikoto, that is, a god of agriculture.

The shrine buildings are in the {{ill|Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Q3155268|qid=Q3155268|lt=Gongen style}}, rebuilt in the 4th year of {{ill|Genroku|ar|فترة غنروكو|cs|Genroku|de|Genroku|es|Genroku|fa|گنروکو|fr|Ère Genroku|id|Genroku|it|Genroku|ja|元禄|ko|겐로쿠|pt|Genroku|ru|Гэнроку|simple|Genroku|sk|Genroku|sr|Генроку|sv|Genroku|tr|Genroku|zh|元祿|qid=Q1325001}} ({{ill|1691|Q7682|qid=Q7682}})<ref>On-site information board</ref>.

===Access===
From {{ill|Sodegaura Station|Q573413|qid=Q573413}}, take a {{ill|Nitto Kotsu|Q11509502|qid=Q11509502|lt=Nitto Kotsu}} bus bound for Nozomino, Hirakawa Administrative Center, or Tokyo German Village, and get off at “Iitomi.”
